No masterclass

Interest has nowhere to go

Someone who connects with a post but isn’t ready to buy a package has one option: a waitlist without a date. Most won’t come back to check.

No application

Your calendar can’t filter

A free discovery call is open to anyone, so your time goes to people who are curious as well as people who are ready.

Price-first choice

Buy now skips the conversation

When six packages sit side by side, people choose on price, before anything has shown them why the 12-session programme might be the right fit.

Anyone not ready to buy today leaves with nothing to say yes to, and no reason to come back.

My recommendation

A free live masterclass between your Instagram and your 1:1 coaching

The class gives people who aren’t ready for coaching a first step, turns your membership into the natural next yes, and shows you who is ready for the 12-session programme.

Fixes the missing entry point

A free class is an easy yes for anyone who follows you, and every sign-up is an email you keep. It gives your waitlist a date and a reason to show up.

Fixes the open calendar

The application on the replay page asks the right questions first, so the calls you take are with people who stayed, listened and want help now.

Makes ads pay for themselves

Membership sign-ups on the thank-you page bring in revenue from day one, and it repeats every month they stay. That covers the ad spend.

The 95%*

Not ready for 1:1 yet

They join the free class, many take the Upside Lifestyle Membership, and your Monday Mindset Calls keep them close. You get paid to build the relationship instead of losing them.

The qualified 5%

Ready for the deeper work

They stay to the end and apply on the replay page. The application filters them before your calendar, and the pre-call emails warm them up for the 12-session programme or the VIP day.

*The 95% / 5% split is an industry estimate, not your data.

Who it’s for

For women ready for the next chapter

  • Women rebuilding after a big change: a loss, a divorce, a redundancy or an empty house.

Meet Caroline

Hi, I’m Caroline Heath

I’m a Resilience & Reinvention Coach. In my 30s I lost both my parents, my only sibling and my whole maternal family. For years I kept a positive front up on the outside while I was struggling on the inside.

Self-development is what turned it around for me. Now I help women go from lost and stuck to confident, excited and living again, through 1:1 coaching and my Upside Lifestyle Membership.

This masterclass is where that work starts.

Script 1 · “Just move on”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“‘Just move on’ might be the least helpful advice there is.”

Body

“In my 30s I lost both my parents and my brother. Everyone wanted me to move on. I didn’t need to move on. I needed to find my next step. Moving forward isn’t forgetting. It’s something you can learn to do, at your own pace.”

CTA

“I’m sharing how in a free live masterclass called Find Your Next Step. Tap Sign up to save your seat.”

Shot: talking to camera, warm natural light, captions on.

Script 2 · “The brave face”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“For years I kept a brave face on for everyone.”

Body

“On the outside I looked fine. On the inside I was stuck. What changed things for me wasn’t pushing harder. It was small daily habits for my mind, body and spirit, and the right support. Those are the same habits I teach my clients now.”

CTA

“I’ll walk you through them in my free 60-minute masterclass. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to on-screen list of the 3 habits.

Script 3 · “What comes next”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Nobody gives you a map for the chapter after a big change.”

Body

“A loss, a divorce, a redundancy, the kids leaving home. When life changes shape, a lot of women lose track of who they are. The good news: a sense of self can be rebuilt. It starts with one clear next step.”

CTA

“Join my free live masterclass, Find Your Next Step. Replay included. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: walking outdoors, then sit down to camera for the CTA.

All ads run with “Educational content, not medical advice.” in the copy, and speak about women in general, never about the viewer’s own circumstances.
